title: The Moon Ferry
story: Every evening, an old ferryman rows a small boat across a lake that reflects the moon. One night a girl arrives carrying a paper star for her absent brother. The ferryman lets the star drift on the water. Its reflection becomes a shining path, and the girl understands that love can travel farther than a boat.
logline: A paper star and a quiet ferryman help a girl send love across a moonlit lake.
characters: Nura — thoughtful girl with a paper star, blue shawl, soft speaking voice. Ferryman — elderly, silver-bearded, patient, speaks rarely.
palette: Deep indigo, moon silver, pale lilac, one amber paper star
voice_plan: Narrator: lyrical and restrained. Nura: one sincere line. Ferryman: no dialogue; communicate through a nod.
music_notes: Slow plucked strings, water-bowl resonance, and a breathy flute. Keep plenty of silence; broaden gently as the reflected path appears.
rights_note: Original procedural preview artwork. Replace or supplement with owned artwork for production.

scenes.title: The evening crossing
scenes.action: A little wooden ferry glides across a still lake. A giant moon shimmers in its reflection.
scenes.narration: Each evening, the ferryman crossed a lake that held the moon.
scenes.sound: Soft oar dip, quiet water, a sparse plucked-string motif.

scenes.title: A paper star
scenes.action: Nura offers the ferryman a paper star. He lowers it to the water; the little star floats beside the boat.
scenes.narration: Nura had brought a small star for someone she missed.
scenes.sound: Paper rustle, one clear water drop, hold a breath of silence.
scenes.transition: Cut from star to its reflection.

scenes.title: A path of light
scenes.action: The star's reflection grows into a silver path across the lake. Nura smiles as the boat follows it toward the far shore.
scenes.narration: The water carried her love farther than any boat could go.
scenes.sound: Flute enters, water brightens, music resolves softly with the boat in silhouette.
